decisions.question: How does TransformEdge represent a pipeline of several stages, a write and a reduceInto, when Spec §6.5 sketches an edge with topic references at both ends?

options.label: Spec sketch literally
options.consequence: one edge per sink whose inputs are the upstream topics; a chain read, map, filter, write cannot be described, so the self-reference check of Spec §3.8 cannot inspect paths and the graph has no internal nodes

options.label: Edges over topic or stage inputs, sinks as edges
options.consequence: an edge's inputs are TopicInput (a read, with its dedup argument) or StageInput (an earlier edge); a write and a reduceInto are sink edges with an output topic; one list carries the whole DAG and keeps the Spec's field names; a write has no CombinatorKind, so combinator is nullable for writes; deviates from the Spec sketch

options.label: Separate sinks list
options.consequence: a sixth definition field for sinks; reduceInto, which has a CombinatorKind and is a sink, straddles both lists; analyses walk two structures

options.label: Sealed edge class per kind
options.consequence: exact typing per combinator, but eighteen or more classes that every consumer switches over and every new combinator breaks

decisions.chosen: Edges over topic or stage inputs, sinks as edges
decisions.why: Spec §3.8 and Guide C.1 define the intra-topology check as inspection of TopologyDefinition.transforms for paths from read to write through stateful operators, so the IR must carry the stage DAG; the Spec sketch cannot. One list with the Spec's field names is the smallest deviation, and CombinatorKind stays at the eighteen values topology-dsl@v1 fixed (a write is the edge with no combinator, validated by three named constructors). The edge also records the read's dedup argument and switchMap's retry reference, because Spec §3.9 makes any observable difference between two activations of one id an error and bus-api@v1 will most likely compare definitions. Signal that would have changed it: consumers that need typed per-kind access often, which would favor a sealed per-kind family.

decisions.question: OQ-M1: How does the recorder name a transformer (FunctionRef) in Dart?

options.label: Derive from toString, VM pattern only
options.consequence: FunctionRef.of reads the name between "from Function '" and the next quote; named on the VM and in AOT, stable obfuscated names under --obfuscate, anonymous on dart2js and dart2wasm and for closures; no DSL change; a static method loses its class

options.label: Derive with a dart2js fallback
options.consequence: names on web builds too, but dart2js names inline closures main_closure and minified builds minified:xx, so closures would get false names

options.label: Explicit name on each combinator
options.consequence: exact names everywhere at the cost of a name argument on every call; a change topology-dsl@v1 lists as not in v1

options.label: Optional explicit name, then derivation, then a positional placeholder
options.consequence: flexible, but placeholders make definition equality depend on stage position and need a topology-dsl@v1 amendment

options.label: Leave naming to the static catalog
options.consequence: definitions from buildDefinition() carry no names, so the runtime graph and the static graph differ, against Spec §6.5's single IR

decisions.chosen: Derive from toString, VM pattern only
decisions.why: The experiment shows JIT and AOT render the names of top-level functions, static methods (without class) and method tear-offs, obfuscated AOT renders stable obfuscated names, dart2js renders compiler-internal names even for inline closures, and dart2wasm renders none. The catalog and the CI checks, which are where names are read, run on the VM; Spec §6.2 makes transformers named standalone functions; topology-dsl@v1's Versioning already answers OQ-M1 by derivation here. Equality is by name, so recording one declaration twice gives equal definitions even with inline closures (topology-dsl@v1 G9). Signal that would have changed it: a v1 consumer needing names in web builds, or static methods of one name in different classes colliding in practice; either brings an optional explicit name as a compatible topology-dsl@v1 addition.

decisions.question: Does the IR carry the durations of debounce, delay, sample and buffer, or does the self-reference analysis treat them as not mediating?

options.label: Carry durations
options.consequence: isStateBearing holds for those four with a positive duration, as topology-dsl@v1's Self-reference column states; graph labels and definition equality see durations

options.label: Treat them as not mediating
options.consequence: a smaller IR, but a debounce feedback loop that Spec §3.8 allows (a stateful chain that cannot loop back in zero time) would be rejected, and topology-dsl@v1's table would need an amendment

decisions.why: topology-dsl@v1 already marks the four stages as mediating when the duration is positive, and Spec §3.8 accepts a stateful chain that cannot loop back in zero time; carrying the duration decides the rule from the IR alone and costs one optional field. A zero duration does not mediate, which the findings sample exercises.

decisions.question: Which public library carries the IR, the graphs, the renderers, the JSON codec and the analyses?

options.label: All in the main library
options.consequence: one import for every consumer; every topology module's namespace also carries renderer, codec and analysis names such as JsonRenderer

options.label: Value types in the main library, the rest in topology_ir.dart
options.consequence: buildDefinition(), which modules call, returns types the main library has; the runtime, tooling and tests import a second library; module namespaces stay small

options.label: Everything in topology_ir.dart
options.consequence: impossible without changing topology-dsl@v1, whose surface fixture uses TopologyDefinition through the main library alone

decisions.chosen: Value types in the main library, the rest in topology_ir.dart
decisions.why: topology-dsl@v1's surface fixture reads TopologyDefinition from the main library, so the value types must be there; nothing in a topology module needs a renderer or an analysis. ADR-002 item 3 lets the declaring contract name a second public library. The case is close: the signal that would have changed it is app topology tests that routinely render graphs, which would favor one library.

decisions.question: Does a definition take reads and writes as arguments, or derive them from its edges?

options.label: Derive them
options.consequence: the constructor takes id, scope and edges; an inconsistent definition cannot exist; the JSON form still lists reads and writes for CI tools, and the decoder rejects a document whose lists disagree with its edges

options.label: Take them as arguments
options.consequence: matches the Spec sketch's five constructor fields and eases hand-built test definitions, but a definition can then contradict its own edges

decisions.why: A pure core should make the inconsistent value unrepresentable; tests build definitions by recording topologies, which yields consistent edges anyway. The redundant lists stay in the JSON form, where CI tools that need only reads and writes per topology (cycles, orphans) read them without walking edges.
evidence: Guide C.3 (topology-graph.json for cycle detection and orphan analysis)

decisions.question: How does a shell publisher's claim and its scope enter the scope-compatibility and single-writer analyses without this contract naming a bus type?

options.label: ShellClaim values inside TopologyGraph
options.consequence: a claim is (MessageSource source, Scope scope defaulting to application, Set<TopicRef> state topics); the graph holds topologies and claims; bus.toGraph() and the catalog build the same type; claims appear as source nodes in renderings, as Spec §3.11 describes

options.label: A separate ownership argument to each analysis
options.consequence: graphs stay topology-only, but every analysis grows a parameter, renderings cannot show shell writers, and the static and live views diverge

options.label: Model claims as pseudo-topologies
options.consequence: no new type, but a claim has no edges or reads, its source is not a topology id, and cycle and self-reference analyses would have to skip them

decisions.why: Spec §3.11 has publisher claims appear as source nodes in the topology graph and Spec §7.2 gives each claimant a scope, application when unbound; one value with those three parts carries exactly that. Writers are identified by MessageSource, the identity their publishes already carry (TopologySource for a topology), so findings name the current owner as Spec §3.11 requires. A claim rejects topology and unknown sources, an empty set and non-state topics, since only state topics are claimed (Spec §2.4).

decisions.question: What does a graph do with two definitions of one topologyId, and with two equal claims?

options.label: Collapse equal definitions, reject unequal ones, keep equal claims
options.consequence: a graph is a map from id to definition, as Spec §3.9 makes the bus; two publishers with one source and one write set stay two claimants, so the single-writer check sees both; the catalog must report duplicate ids before building a graph

options.label: Keep every definition and report duplicates as a finding
options.consequence: the catalog gets a diagnostic for free, but every analysis keyed by topology id becomes ambiguous and the check is not in root D1's v1 list

options.label: Collapse equal claims too
options.consequence: set semantics throughout, but two identical publisher constructions, a real runtime first-claim failure, would pass the static single-writer check

decisions.chosen: Collapse equal definitions, reject unequal ones, keep equal claims
decisions.why: Spec §3.9: activating one id twice with the same declaration is the same topology, with a different one an error, so the graph mirrors the bus. Spec §3.11's runtime first-claim rejects a second publisher even when it is identical to the first, so the static view must count it. Signal that would have changed it: catalogs that legitimately hold one id in two coordination domains.

decisions.question: What shape do the analyses take: what they consume, what they return, and which checks are here?

options.label: One function per analysis over TopologyGraph, typed findings in a sealed family, plus analyzeTopologyGraph
options.consequence: cycles, self-references, writer conflicts and scope violations as final classes under sealed TopologyFinding, a fixed result order, topic name collisions over caller-supplied TopicDeclaration values; the runtime and the workspace scan call the same functions

options.label: Methods on TopologyGraph returning strings
options.consequence: compact, but untyped diagnostics that bus-api@v1 and nidana-checks@v1 would each parse

options.label: Leave single-writer to the runtime and the scan
options.consequence: matches nidana.model's Owns list literally, but ADR-002 item 8 has the scan run single-writer by calling the contracts package's analyses, the functions activation also calls

decisions.chosen: One function per analysis over TopologyGraph, typed findings in a sealed family, plus analyzeTopologyGraph
decisions.why: Root D4 and ADR-002 item 8 require activation and CI to run the same pure functions; typed sealed findings let both hosts map them to diagnostics exhaustively. Single-writer is included because ADR-002 item 8 lists it among the analyses the scan calls; nidana.model's Owns list should name it (note for the orchestrator). The guarantee that a finding-free graph stays finding-free when topologies or claims are removed (G17) lets the bus keep its active set clean by rejecting any activation or publisher whose graph has a finding.

decisions.question: What exactly is an unmediated self-read, and what does a SelfReference finding report?

options.label: Paths of non-state-bearing edges from a read to a write of the topic, every edge on them reported
options.consequence: well defined whatever the algorithm (forward reach from the read intersected with backward reach from the write); a withLatestFrom over the topology's own state is unmediated, as topology-dsl@v1's column marks it

options.label: Report one representative path
options.consequence: a shorter diagnostic, but which path is algorithm-dependent and untestable as a value

options.label: Treat a latest input of withLatestFrom as mediating
options.consequence: accepts the reducer-by-withLatestFrom pattern, which cannot loop in zero time, but contradicts topology-dsl@v1's Self-reference column and the reduceInto idiom Spec §6.3 provides

decisions.chosen: Paths of non-state-bearing edges from a read to a write of the topic, every edge on them reported
decisions.why: Spec §3.8 asks that any read of a self-written topic reach the write only through a state-bearing operator; the set of edges on unmediated paths is unique, so the finding is a value the fixtures can pin. topology-dsl@v1 fixed which stages mediate, and reduceInto is the DSL's reducer. Signal that would have changed it: real topologies that need withLatestFrom over their own state.

decisions.question: What counts as a topic name collision (Spec §4.3)?

options.label: Any two distinct declarations of one name
options.consequence: two registries declaring cart.items fail CI even with one type; the input carries a caller-chosen site so equal declarations from two places stay distinct

options.label: Only declarations whose variant or type differ
options.consequence: mirrors the runtime check, but two teams silently sharing a channel by accident would pass

decisions.chosen: Any two distinct declarations of one name
decisions.why: Spec §4.3 says the CI step fails the build on any name collision and names the runtime type check as defense in depth only.

decisions.question: Are the JSON form of a single definition and the aggregated topology-graph.json one schema or two?

options.label: One schema, one document type
options.consequence: the graph document is the only top-level form; a single definition's JSON is the object a graph document lists ($defs/topologyDefinition); one decoder entry point and one format string

options.label: Two schemas, the graph one referencing the definition one
options.consequence: a standalone definition document exists, at the cost of cross-file $ref resolution in two validators and two formats to version

options.label: One schema whose root is either form
options.consequence: both documents validate at the root, but every consumer must branch on which it got

decisions.why: Spec §6.5 renders the JSON form from the graph (graph.render(JsonRenderer())), and nothing in v1 emits a lone definition document; a graph of one definition (toGraph()) covers that use. One document keeps the CI consumers' contract to one format.

decisions.question: Who emits the aggregated topology-graph.json, and through which contract?

options.label: nidana.tooling through topic-codegen@v1
options.consequence: the file contract names the path and generator command; the content is JsonRenderer of the catalog's graph, byte for byte, so the file replay compares it like any generated file; nidana-checks@v1's scan builds or reads the same graph

options.label: nidana.tooling through nidana-checks@v1
options.consequence: the scan writes the manifest as a side output of a cli contract, whose recorded invocations compare stdout and exit codes, not generated trees

decisions.why: Guide C.3 lists topology-graph.json among the codegen's emitted artifacts, and ADR-002 item 8 has the workspace scan share the topology catalog with graph emission, so both read one graph. Signal that would have changed it: an app that runs the checks without running the codegen.

decisions.question: Is the JSON form closed or open to unknown keys, and how strict is the decoder about order?

options.label: Closed schema with a format string, canonical encoder, order-lenient decoder
options.consequence: every object has additionalProperties false, format is topology-ir@v1, so a v1 decoder never misreads another version; any added key is a v2; the encoder sorts set-like lists, the decoder accepts any order

options.label: Open schema, consumers ignore unknown keys
options.consequence: additive evolution within v1, but invalid/ cases lose their bite, typos pass, and a v2 document may be silently half-read

options.label: Closed and order-strict
options.consequence: one document per graph enforced at decode, but hand-edited or reordered documents fail for no semantic reason

decisions.chosen: Closed schema with a format string, canonical encoder, order-lenient decoder
decisions.why: The contract is versioned, so additions bump the version anyway; a closed schema makes the 38 invalid/ cases meaningful and the format string makes version skew loud. Canonical encoding keeps topology-graph.json byte-stable for the file contract; leniency on order costs nothing semantic. Signal that would have changed it: an external CI consumer that needs additive fields within v1.

decisions.question: How precisely does the contract fix the Mermaid and Graphviz renderings?

options.label: Exact rules pinned by goldens
options.consequence: node ids, labels, shapes, arrow order and escaping are stated and every sample's text is a golden, so consumers that embed or diff renderings (the build-time HTML graph, docs) build against fixed text; any rendering change is a v2

options.label: Structural guarantees only
options.consequence: layout freedom for the producer, but consumers' own goldens would depend on text no contract fixes

decisions.why: Determinism is what makes generated documentation and the build-time graph reviewable, and HSDD wants the fixtures to be the mocks. Every edge, a write included, is a node inside its topology's subgraph, so every arrow to a topic names the topology that writes it. All seven Mermaid goldens parse with Mermaid 11.12.0 and all seven DOT goldens lay out with Graphviz 14.0.1, and undoing the escapes makes both fail. Signal that would have changed it: a renderer consumer that wants layout freedom more than stable text.

decisions.question: What is the signature of expectMatchesSchema, which ADR-001 item 4 names but does not type, and how do conformance cases find the schema and the valid/, invalid/ and render/ files?

options.label: expectMatchesSchema(Object? instance, String schemaPath), paths relative to the workspace root found by walking up
options.consequence: explicit, greppable paths; a binding works from the root and from a member's directory (a consumer stand-in, ADR-001 item 11); nidana.model's first phase implements it on package:json_schema

options.label: expectMatchesSchema(instance, slug: ...)
options.consequence: layout-independent call sites, but a fixture cannot validate against a schema at another path, and the slug-to-path rule is hidden in the tool

options.label: The harness supplies files and schemas
options.consequence: no I/O in the conformance library, but every binding repeats file plumbing and could supply a subset

decisions.chosen: expectMatchesSchema(Object? instance, String schemaPath), paths relative to the workspace root found by walking up
decisions.why: ADR-001 item 9 runs bindings from the workspace root, and item 11 lets consumers bind suites from their own package; walking up to the directory that holds hsdd/contract/ serves both, as T10 of the experiment shows. The signature is the one fixture.dart addition this contract needs from the replay tool.

decisions.question: How are the serialized-form fixtures laid out: where do valid/ documents come from, what do invalid/ documents mutate, and where do rendering goldens live?

options.label: Recorded samples as goldens, one small base for invalid/, render/ data files
options.consequence: each valid/ file is the producer's JsonRenderer output for a sample graph the conformance library records with the DSL, so G19 checks real output byte for byte; each invalid/ file breaks one rule of valid/forms.json; render/ holds .mmd and .dot files the behavior set reads, outside ADR-001's named sets

options.label: Hand-written valid/ documents, goldens as Dart strings
options.consequence: no data directory beyond ADR-001's sets, but the producer's output is never compared with a file, and renderings are unreadable in review

decisions.chosen: Recorded samples as goldens, one small base for invalid/, render/ data files
decisions.why: ADR-001 item 4 asks the conformance library to check the producer's real output; recording the samples and comparing exact files does that and pins the projection, the naming and the encoding at once. A 2.8 kB base keeps each invalid/ case reviewable, and each was checked to fail at the intended path under two validators. The binding is named nidana_dart_contracts_test.dart after the implementing package, as topic-model@v1's is; case names follow S06 and S07's convention. The goldens were written by the stand-in and then read; a stand-in defect would have entered them, which T14 cannot catch, so the review was by reading each file.

experiments.question: What does Function.toString() carry for each function form a declaration can pass, under JIT, AOT, obfuscated AOT, dart2js -O1 and -O4, and dart2wasm, and what does a derivation from it yield?
experiments.finding: JIT and AOT render 'from Function NAME' for top-level functions, static methods (no class), instance method tear-offs, generic functions, constructor tear-offs ('Box.') and implicit call tear-offs ('call'); inline closures, closures in variables, local named functions and extension method tear-offs render no name. --obfuscate keeps the pattern with obfuscated names stable within the build. dart2js renders 'Closure NAME' with compiler-internal names even for inline closures (main_closure) and minified names at -O4; dart2wasm renders no name at all. The VM-pattern derivation is therefore anonymous on web builds and never false.

experiments.question: Do the topology-ir@v1 fixtures and schema hold against a stand-in that implements the Interface, and do topology-dsl@v1's fixtures still hold against the stand-in's projection?
experiments.finding: Against a stand-in of nidana_dart_contracts implementing this Interface (its recorder's plan projection rewritten to the contract's rules): the structure prototype covers all 22 guarantees (41 cases, 1 binding); both surface libraries analyze clean under --fatal-infos; all three reject files report exactly their marked (line, code) pairs, every code confirmed on first write; package:json_schema 5.2.2 and Ajv 8.17.1 (strict) agree that the 7 valid/ files validate and the 38 invalid/ files fail, each at the intended path; the binding passes all 41 cases from the root and from a member directory; the 7 Mermaid goldens parse with Mermaid 11.12.0 and the 7 DOT goldens lay out with Graphviz 14.0.1, and undoing the escapes makes both fail; the Interface example validates and round-trips; regenerating goldens reproduces the committed files; each of 22 seeded defects in the stand-in fails the cases of the guarantee it breaks (two mutations that first survived led to a tightened G6 case, a new G7 case and a replaced G13 mutation); adding a CombinatorKind value fails the surface set; topology-dsl@v1's structure, surface, reject and recording sets still pass against the new projection.

notes_for_orchestrator: OQ-M1 is decided here: FunctionRef.of(f) takes the name the Dart VM renders in f.toString() (the text between "from Function '" and the next "'"), anonymous otherwise; equality by name; no explicit name parameter in v1 (topology-dsl@v1 Versioning already says so). Landing: topology-ir@v1 Interface 'Function references' and G9, evidence docs/auto-run/experiments/function-ref-derivation/. hsdd/spec/nidana.model.md cannot be edited by this step: its OQ-M1 row should become RESOLVED (2026-10-17): topology-ir@v1 G9 at nidana.model's next step or the reconcile sweep. OQ-M2: this contract confirms topology-dsl@v1 refinement 3 (the IR stays pure data, G4), so that row can be swept too.

For S09 (bus-api@v1), activation checks: build TopologyGraph(topologies: the active definitions plus the candidate's plan.definition, claims: every live publisher as ShellClaim(source, scope bound or application, writes)), call analyzeTopologyGraph and reject on any finding; G17 keeps a finding-free active set finding-free under deactivation and disposal, so any finding involves the candidate. Publisher construction runs the same check with the new claim. Findings are typed values that the D8 diagnostics and the throws can carry; WriterConflict.writers names the current owner as Spec §3.11 requires.

For S09: TopologyGraph throws ArgumentError for two unequal definitions with one topologyId, so idempotency (Spec §3.9) must be decided before the graph is built. Definition equality (G7) covers structure, kinds, function names, durations, dedup and retry, but not a scan's initial value, closure bodies, or two functions rendering one name; bus-api@v1 must say whether equal definitions mean 'the same declaration'.

For S09: bus.toGraph() returns this contract's TopologyGraph; recommendation: include the live publishers' claims, so the live graph shows shell writers as the static one does (Spec §3.11). ShellClaim accepts only service, page and executor sources and only state topics; bus.publisher's API must map onto that or reject.

For topic-codegen@v1: name the path and generator command of topology-graph.json; its content is const JsonRenderer().render(graph) of the catalog's TopologyGraph, byte-stable (canonical order, two-space indent, final newline), so its expected/ tree can hold it. The build-time HTML graph can embed MermaidRenderer output. The catalog must run on the VM without --obfuscate, or FunctionRef names are obfuscated.

For nidana-checks@v1: the workspace scan builds the catalog's TopologyGraph with ShellClaims extracted from bus.publisher(...) constructions (source via MessageSource.tryParse, writes, bound scope or application), calls analyzeTopologyGraph and findTopicNameCollisions(TopicDeclaration(topic, site)) with a file:line site; it must report duplicate topology ids itself before building the graph (the graph throws); unresolvable claim sets stay warnings outside the graph (Spec §3.11).

Changes needed in topic-model@v1 or topology-dsl@v1: none. Every topology-dsl@v1 fixture set that needs no live bus still passes against a stand-in implementing this contract's projection (experiment T15).

Follow-up for nidana.model (node spec, next step or reconcile): its Owns list names four analyses; add single-writer over topology writes and shell claims (findWriterConflicts, Spec §3.11), which ADR-002 item 8 and this contract place in the model.

Follow-up for nidana.model's first phase (replay tool): implement expectMatchesSchema(Object? instance, String schemaPath) in package:nidana_contract_check/fixture.dart as topology-ir@v1's Validation states (paths relative to the workspace root found by walking up), and the schema set over valid/ and invalid/; the structure set must tolerate the render/ data directory, which ADR-001 names no set for.

Marked would_upstream: Spec §6.5's TransformEdge sketch cannot describe multi-stage pipelines (decision 1); Spec §3.8's state-bearing rule is made precise as positive-duration debounce, delay, sample and buffer (decision 3) and a withLatestFrom over the topology's own state as unmediated (decision 9). Appendix A.4 names CombineLatest where topology-dsl@v1 named combine; no new action.

Known fixture assumption: the G3 reject codes assume the Interface's getters are final fields (assignment_to_final); a getter-only implementation reports assignment_to_final_no_setter. Recorded in Validation, as a gap the first replay would surface.
